title: Airborne selected by Airbus to assess composite rotor blade automation
summary: Airborne has signed an agreement with Airbus to explore advanced composite automation at Airbus Helicopters’ Paris-Le Bourget rotor blade manufacturing facility.
body_markdown:
Airborne has signed an agreement with Airbus to explore advanced composite automation at Airbus Helicopters’ Paris-Le Bourget rotor blade manufacturing facility.


The technology aims to strengthen industrial efficiency and scalability to meet growing global demand for Airbus helicopters.


Airbus Helicopters’ Paris-Le Bourget site serves as the company’s Centre of Excellence for rotor blades, bringing together composite blade engineering, manufacturing and repair. The site continues to adopt next-generation manufacturing processes to enhance quality, repeatability and material efficiency across its rotorcraft programmes.


The new project will assess the possibility to introduce Airborne’s Automated Ply Placement (APP) and Airborne’s Kit by Light (KBL) technologies into the Paris-Le Bourget production environment, as part of a broader evaluation of industry solutions.


Should this initial evaluation prove successful, it could lead to the deployment of APP and KBL systems to support a more connected and adaptable production flow, combining material efficiency, repeatability and digital process control with the flexibility required for complex blade manufacturing.


“For us, this project is about more than automating individual production steps,” said Paul Vorstermans, CEO at Airborne. “It is about demonstrating how we can enable Airbus to create a more responsive manufacturing process that can scale with increasing demand, while maintaining the quality, flexibility and control required in aerospace production. By building on our technologies already proven elsewhere within Airbus, we aim to help validate that next step.”


**Creating a more flexible and scalable production flow**


Airborne’s Automated Ply Placement technology automates the creation of composite laminates and preforms by cutting, picking and accurately placing individual plies. The software-driven system can process prepreg, dry fibre and thermoplastic materials and is designed for high-mix production without requiring conventional robot programming.


Kit by Light digitalizes cutting and kitting operations, connecting production demand to material cutting, nesting and kit preparation. The system guides operators through the process while improving material utilization, productivity and traceability.


**Enabled by Dutch industrial participation**


The project has been supported by the Dutch Ministry of Economic Affairs and builds on long-term industrial cooperation between Dutch technology companies and international aerospace manufacturers, helping advanced manufacturing technologies move from development into operational production environments.


*This press release was prepared and distributed by Airborne.*
